sectors.trend: Middle East oil shock risk; petrol price shock hitting consumers; Japan absorbing Australian LNG, starving East Coast; coal policy uncertainty
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, BRL.AX, XVG.AX benefit from oil/LNG price spikes; downstream refiners (VIL.AX) squeezed; renewable transition delayed by Victoria backing away from transmission projects

sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX remain defensive anchors; super reform debate may redirect fund allocation toward healthcare/defensive equities

Middle East oil shock and global energy price volatility

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA rate hike / IMF fiscal tightening
risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight short-duration bonds; reduce leverage; favour rate-sensitive financials (CBA.AX, NAB.AX) that benefit from NIM expansion

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Middle East oil shock / petrol price spike
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge energy exposure via WDS.AX, BRL.AX; reduce consumer discretionary; monitor AUD/USD for import-cost pass-through
Shift toward defensive sectors (CSL.AX, WES.AX, utilities); reduce cyclical mining exposure; maintain cash buffer
Underweight BHP.AX, FMG.AX near-term; rotate into gold (AUR.AX, FOR.AX) and diversified miners
Avoid QAN.AX until resolution; monitor transport/aviation supply chain disruption
Selective REIT exposure only; favour industrial/healthcare REITs over residential; monitor tenant relief policy impact

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold exploration and production names
opportunities.rationale: Forrestania four prefeasibility studies and Aurum high-grade Côte d'Ivoire discovery signal sector upcycle; gold benefits from rate-hike and geopolitical risk

opportunities.recommendation: Add to big four banks on rate-hike expectations
opportunities.rationale: RBA warning and IMF pressure suggest further hikes; NIM expansion supports earnings; banks already advancing on easing yields

opportunities.recommendation: Position in energy producers ahead of oil shock
opportunities.rationale: Middle East oil shock risk and petrol price surge support upstream earnings; LNG constraint to Japan tightens domestic supply
Anthropic $31bn Queensland deal signals sustained hyperscaler capex into Australia; AI advisory sector expanding

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce cyclical mining and consumer discretionary exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Iron ore weakness, recession odds rising, and petrol shock compress consumer spending; housing unaffordability caps REIT upside

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain defensive healthcare and staples allocation
defensive_moves.rationale: CSL.AX and WES.AX provide earnings visibility amid macro uncertainty; super reform debate may redirect fund flows to defensives
Fed rate hike, oil shock, and recession fears pressure AUD; import-cost pass-through risks inflation reacceleration

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain volatile and range-bound. RBA rate decision and IMF fiscal pressure create headwinds, but bank strength and energy upside provide support. Qantas strike and oil shock are near-term catalysts for volatility. Expect ^AXJO to trade in a tight band with sector rotation from materials to financials/energy.
market_outlook.long_term: 2027 recession risk is the dominant medium-term concern. Housing affordability, state interest costs, and immigration tightening constrain growth. However, gold upcycle, datacentre capex, and potential RBA pivot after peak rates offer selective opportunities. Structural shift toward defensive and tech-infrastructure themes.
